technique.how: Curvilinear/phased-array probe, patient supine: right upper quadrant (hepatorenal/Morison pouch, including the inferior liver tip and right paracolic gutter), left upper quadrant (splenorenal and subphrenic), and pelvis (retrovesical/pouch of Douglas, transverse and sagittal, ideally with bladder full). Look for anechoic stripes between organs; add subxiphoid cardiac view for the full FAST.
technique.prerequisites: Trained operator; patient supine (Trendelenburg increases RUQ yield); serial repeat scans if initial scan negative and suspicion persists.
technique.contraindications: None; must not delay resuscitation or transfer to laparotomy in the unstable trauma patient.

interpretation.positive_finding: Free fluid in a blunt-trauma patient markedly raises the probability of intra-abdominal injury; with hypotension it usually indicates hemoperitoneum warranting laparotomy. In non-trauma patients free fluid is nonspecific (ascites, ruptured viscus, ruptured AAA, ectopic).
interpretation.negative_finding: A negative FAST lowers but does not exclude intra-abdominal injury (sensitivity ~0.7); retroperitoneal, solid-organ, and hollow-viscus injuries are missed and CT or serial exams are needed when suspicion persists.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sensitivity is worse in children and early after injury before fluid accumulates; pre-existing ascites, urine from bladder rupture, and pleural fluid or perinephric fat can be mistaken for hemoperitoneum. FAST detects fluid, not the source, and cannot diagnose SBP or AAA.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive in unstable blunt trauma: OR/laparotomy or embolization; negative with persisting concern: CT or serial FAST. In non-trauma, positive fluid prompts paracentesis/CT for cause.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: intra-abdominal injury (positive bedside ultrasound = intraperitoneal free fluid OR organ injury)
estimates.population: Adult ED patients with blunt abdominal trauma; 22 bedside ultrasound studies pooled (RCE)
estimates.reference_standard: Abdominal CT, diagnostic peritoneal lavage, laparotomy, autopsy and/or clinical course
estimates.quote: (adjusted summary LR, 30; 95% CI, 20-46); conversely, a normal ultrasound result decreases the chance of injury detection (adjusted summary LR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.19-0.34)

estimates.target_condition: Abdominal injury (free fluid/organ injury) in blunt trauma, POCS/FAST, abdominal-trauma subgroup
estimates.population: Blunt-trauma patients of any age, civilian; 34 studies, 8635 participants overall (abdominal subgroup estimate)
estimates.reference_standard: CT, MRI, laparoscopy/laparotomy, thoracoscopy/thoracotomy, autopsy, or combination
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.68/(1-0.95) = 13.6; LR- = (1-0.68)/0.95 = 0.34 from reported pooled sens/spec
estimates.quote: For abdominal trauma, POCS had a sensitivity of 0.68 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.75) and a specificity of 0.95 (95% CI 0.92 to 0.97).

sources.citation: Nishijima DK, Simel DL, Wisner DH, Holmes JF. Does this adult patient have a blunt intra-abdominal injury? JAMA. 2012.

Stengel D, Leisterer J, Ferrada P, Ekkernkamp A, Mutze S, Hoenning A. Point-of-care ultrasonography for diagnosing thoracoabdominal injuries in patients with blunt trauma. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2018.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative FAST to discharge or to stop the work-up of a blunt-trauma patient with ongoing concern, in children, or in penetrating trauma; do not use to diagnose SBP, AAA rupture, or the source of ascites.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Positive FAST with hypotension in trauma is a surgical emergency; free fluid with peritonitis or unexplained shock in non-trauma patients needs immediate surgical/imaging evaluation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Accuracy varies markedly by operator, population and body region across the 34 Cochrane studies; no pooled kappa reported in the abstracts reviewed.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency/critical-care clinician credentialed in FAST (e.g., ACEP-level training with supervised scans); estimates derive from trained trauma-center operators and do not transfer to novices.

extraction_notes: RCE (PMID 22496266) pools 'intraperitoneal fluid or organ injury on bedside ultrasound', hence COMPOSITE label; adult blunt-trauma prevalence 0.13 (95% CI 10%-17%) from the same abstract. Cochrane 2018 (PMID 30548249): overall thoracoabdominal pooled sens 0.74 (0.65-0.81), spec 0.96 (0.94-0.98), LR+ 18.5 (10.8-40.5), LR- 0.27 (0.19-0.37); children sens 0.63 (0.46-0.77) vs adult/mixed 0.78 (0.69-0.84), spec 0.91 vs 0.97; median pretest probability 28% (all Abstract, Main results) - not entered as separate rows because they include chest injuries. Cochrane DOI not returned by the tool; PMID confirmed. No diagnostic-accuracy data for free fluid in non-trauma differentials (cirrhosis/SBP/AAA/perforation) were sought within budget; these mappings rest on physiology, not on FAST accuracy studies. Operator level in pooled data is heterogeneous (emergency physicians, surgeons, radiologists).
